title: Taskbase 2019–2023 — monorepo homepage
stack: Angular 14.2.12 (started at 5, via 6/9/12/13), Bootstrap 4.5, node 14, SCSS
build: docker node:14 + @angular/cli 14.2.10, driven from the monorepo root as it was at f66d393bea (root package.json / angular.json / tsconfig.json / polyfills.ts plus common, aila-sdk, aila-common, building, homepage, extracted with git archive): npm ci, npm install in homepage/client, then "ng build homepage --configuration production --base-href ./". The two generated typing files (common/client/ai/ai-dto.generated.ts, common/client/lap-sdk-types/internal/lap-sdk-types.generated.ts) come from a Gradle "generateTypeScript" step that needs the whole Kotlin backend, so they were stubbed: 242 names, each a type alias to any plus a Proxy value so enum uses resolve. noImplicitAny/strictNullChecks off, and one lodash callback in common/client task code needed an explicit any.
notes: A real Angular 14 production build of the monorepo source at f66d393be, not a reconstruction: the April-2018 look grown up, techmodul became a technology section, no more Google Maps on the team page, six demos, new portraits, the Dreikoenigstrasse 47 address. Every route renders: team, impressum, technology/<link>, examples/*. The two Gradle-generated DTO typing files are still stubbed (242 names, each a type alias to any plus a Proxy whose keys are their own values) because generateTypeScript needs the whole Kotlin backend compiled — but that is invisible here. Only four files use a stubbed name as a value, and each first needs an answer from a backend that no longer exists: the demos post to a gateway, the grammar task logs into LAP. Comparisons inside the app are stub against stub and stay self-consistent; nothing on screen depends on a real enum literal. Now fully offline: gateway.taskbase.com, lap.taskbase.com and the contact form's Firebase function point at a local not-archived/ path, and the Google Fonts the build left live (a gstatic @import plus 14 inlined faces) are vendored locally. Two genuine 2023 bugs are kept: the "browser version no longer supported" snackbar, which compares versions as strings so Chrome "141" sorts below its 2016 floor — and which will not dismiss, because the original app.module never imported BrowserAnimationsModule; and the postcard demo's missing assets/img/postcard.svg, a file that never existed at this commit.
